ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a trapezoid QRTU, QR is the upper base, UT is the lower base; V is located on the left leg QU, S is located on the right leg RT, and segment VS horizontally connects the points on the two legs and is parallel to the two bases. The problem states that V and S are the midpoints of the two legs, and TU = 26, SV = 17. Reasoning: In a trapezoid, the segment connecting the midpoints of the two legs is the midline, whose length is equal to the average of the lengths of the two bases. Therefore SV = (QR + TU) / 2. Substitute SV = 17, TU = 26, obtaining 17 = (QR + 26) / 2. Multiply both sides by 2: 34 = QR + 26, so QR = 8.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as trapezoid QRTU with top base QR, bottom base TU, and segment VS connecting points on the two non-parallel legs. From the text, V and S are midpoints of the legs, TU = 26, and SV = 17. Use the trapezoid midsegment theorem: the segment joining the midpoints of the legs is parallel to the bases and has length equal to the average of the base lengths. Set SV = (QR + TU)/2, so 17 = (QR + 26)/2, then solve QR = 8.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a trapezoid with horizontal bases QR and TU, and with V on leg QU and S on leg RT. From the text, V and S are the midpoints of the legs, TU = 26, and SV = 17. Use a coordinate/averaging setup: place the lower base TU on a horizontal line with length 26 and the upper base QR on a parallel horizontal line with unknown length x. Because V and S are midpoints of the two legs, their horizontal separation is the average of the horizontal separations of the corresponding endpoints, so SV = (x + 26)/2. Substitute SV = 17 to get 17 = (x + 26)/2 and solve x = 8, hence QR = 8.
